prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: a single part on B008 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case is the chain from physiology to medicine. Holst showed GLP-1 secretion and its insulinotropic action in humans, Mojsov identified the biologically active truncated peptide, and Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology. That work produced a drug class whose glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefits have been replicated in large independent outcome trials over about two decades. The mechanism is settled and the field is mature. Round 1 raised no maturity objection from any member, and no one disputed the scientific chain. I do not count the unanimity as an argument. What I weigh is that the originality sits in physiology and the verified impact is large.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point. The credited list has four names for three slots, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener and colleagues cannot be settled from the supplied material, and a trio of discoverers leaves out Knudsen, whose long-acting analogues are what patients receive. A citation anchored in the physiology can look as if it stops before the drugs. Durability and long-term safety of weight loss are still accumulating, though that does not touch the core discovery. I also accept that if the committee defines the achievement as the arc to therapy, my trio would be the wrong one.

responses.point: She proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a citation covering both the physiology and the development of incretin therapies. She would accept Mojsov in the third slot if the committee records a narrowing to discovery biology.
responses.response: Your argument that the drugs are what changed medicine is the strongest case for a different configuration, and I have weighed it again. I keep Mojsov, for two reasons. First, the question of which step the later pharmacology depended on has a clear answer. Without a defined, active target peptide there was no compound to stabilise, so identification of the active form is upstream of analogue design. Second, the committee's usual practice is to credit the discovery and describe the medicine it enabled. I have therefore worded my citation so that it reaches the therapies: 'made incretin-based therapies possible'. That answers your concern in the citation without dropping a basic discoverer. I agree your preference should be recorded as a view on scope and not as an error. If the committee concludes that Mojsov's priority is too disputed to defend, Knudsen is the credible replacement, and I would accept that over leaving the third slot unresolved.

responses.point: As chair he keeps Mojsov but says he would not block Knudsen if her priority is judged too disputed. He also raises whether a single large achievement crowds out CAR-T, SMA antisense therapy and HPV vaccination.
responses.response: I share your position on the Mojsov and Knudsen question and also cannot resolve priority from the supplied files. That is a reason to be open about the uncertainty. It is not a reason to change the trio, because the committee has no evidence that her claim is weaker than the others. On crowding out, I do not think a second part should be added just to make room for the next candidate. A second part is justified only if it meets the same standard of attribution and maturity as B008. None of the alternatives meets that standard yet, so I do not see a reason to split the prize this year. If the committee wants a second part, B017 limited to a clean pair is closer than B034. That would require removing someone from the B008 trio, because of the three-person ceiling, and I would not support that.

responses.point: She anchors the citation in physiology and the active peptide, and says emerging neurological benefit should not count in the case because it is not established. She treats B034 as a serious alternative but less ready than B008.
responses.response: I agree that the case should rest on the established glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes. I leave neurological effects out of my argument as well. On B034 I accept your point and have shifted. In round 1 I put it first among alternatives, but I now rank B017 ahead of it. Your argument that a Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth selection needs a rule separating the discovery of channelrhodopsin from the neuronal deployment has not been answered by anyone, including me. I can state that such a rule can be defended in principle, but I cannot show that it would not look arbitrary toward Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck. I still regard the work as a major discovery for circuit neuroscience, and I do not accept that a method cannot qualify. My concern is attribution, not the nature of the work.

responses.point: He treats CAR-T as strong but questions the third name. He regards Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer as a separate line from CAR design and Eshhar's absence as a gap, and he does not see nusinersen as a rival this year.
responses.response: The Rosenberg and Eshhar problems you and others describe change my ranking. I now put B017 above B034 as first alternative, since a pair of June and Sadelain is defensible on maturity and clinical effect, and the gap for Eshhar is one question and not six. I also agree that nusinersen is a credible later prize. It has a single disease and a single platform, and its length of use is shorter than that of incretin therapy. That is why it is not my alternative this year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide holds against Habener and colleagues. I cannot verify this from the supplied files, and it determines whether she or Knudsen takes the third slot.
Whether the committee wants the citation to cover only the physiology or also the development of analogue therapies. The wording 'made possible' leaves that open.
Whether a June and Sadelain B017 prize can be allocated fairly while Eshhar's chimeric-receptor concept lies outside the credited names.
Whether durability and long-term safety of weight loss will alter the clinical picture. I do not think they affect the discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal is apparent for B008, B017, B034 or any other shortlisted candidate. B034 concerns neural circuit tools in my broad field, but my profile documents no personal or institutional tie to any credited name. My documented connections to Sten Grillner, Patrik Ernfors and Thomas Perlmann (a 2009 co-authored paper on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons) do not involve any shortlisted candidate or credited name.
